raw.query: WITH latency_info AS ( SELECT DISTINCT l.window_name, l.p99_ms AS observed_delay, e.handoff_p99_ms AS observed_handoff FROM provenance.v_pool_latency l JOIN provenance.encoder_run_summary e ON l.run_id = e.run_id WHERE l.experiment = 'a2' AND l.policy = 'forecast' AND l.window_name IN ('burst1', 'burst3', 'burst4', 'burst5') AND l.sla_metric = 'encoder_delay' AND l.is_current = true ), forward_info AS ( SELECT aic_pred_ms AS observed_forward FROM provenance.collector_encoder_fn WHERE engine = 'sdpa' AND n_images = 64 AND is_valid = true LIMIT 1 ) SELECT li.window_name, li.observed_delay, li.observed_handoff, fi.observed_forward FROM latency_info li CROSS JOIN forward_info fi;
raw.observed: delay = 588.37 ms, handoff = 272.001 ms, forward = 316.369 ms
raw.claimed: p90 schedule p99 encoder delay = 588 ms = 316.4 ms (full-batch forward) + 272 ms (p99 handoff transfer)
raw.evidence: In the headline closed-loop experiment a2 (the p90 forecast schedule), the p99 encoder delay across all four burst windows (burst1, burst3, burst4, burst5) is exactly 588.37 ms (rounds to 588 ms), which decomposes perfectly into a full-batch forward latency of 316.369 ms and a p99 handoff transfer latency of 272.001 ms. The prior refutation was flawed because it incorrectly queried the superseded exploratory 'ctmatrix' experiment rather than the headline experiment 'a2' which is the subject of the text.
